events.excerpt: Your first Ethereum Classic node, part 2: run core-geth with Docker In Part 1 , I showed you how to set up core-geth by building it from the source we got from GitHub. This time, we're going to use Docker. Docker is a containerization tool. In layman's terms, it lets you spin up little self-contained boxes called containers on your machine and run them separately, for as long as you need them. Each container comes with everything its software needs to run. So instead of building core-geth yourself, you just download a ready-made image of it and run it. events.excerpt: Run your own Ethereum Classic node, part 1: build core-geth from source Running a node is one of the most significant ways anyone can contribute to Ethereum Classic. Every node keeps its own copy of the blockchain, a record of every block, transaction and smart contract. More nodes make ETC more decentralized and the network more resilient, plus it lets you interact with the network without relying on a trusted third party. It's also easier to set up than you might think, and this guide will show you how, step-by-step.
